title: Rock and roll and what dancers want
summary: Asked about Black audiences, he says young people favor rock and roll, but dance music is what pays and what you must play.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

They used to go, the color used to go for all that. But now they don't go for that. They don't want all that little rock and roll stuff. And now I don't see no sense in it. All they're just doing is killing yourself. They're killing themselves. They're jumping around you, they're soaking wet.
They be soaking wet. You understand? You can't play the kind of music for them. They say, oh,
we want you to play regular style music. Dance music where they can dance.

They want dance music. You understand me? What many people tell you that? They don't want to have to tell you that twice. You understand? They come back and just stop you. So if you can't play it, don't play at all. You're feeling bad. You can't play what you want. You got to play what them people want. And when you satisfy the people in the audience, when you're playing music, that's the best thing in the world. Now, you don't go there to play music for yourself like you want. No. You don't be doing that. You got to play to satisfy them people.
